scenarios.title: Opening after a long hold
scenarios.situation: Customer waited over six minutes on hold and sounds impatient.
targetPhrases: Thanks for waiting—I know your time is valuable.
This is [Name] with [Company]. How can I help today?
You’re in the right place.
First, may I quickly verify your full name and email?
I’ll take care of this for you.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Agent acknowledges the wait in the first 10 seconds, delivers a branded greeting with their name, verifies two data points, and moves into the issue in under 30 seconds with a calm, friendly tone.

scenarios.title: Third transfer recovery
scenarios.situation: Customer has been transferred twice and expects to repeat the story again.
targetPhrases: I’m sorry you’ve had to repeat yourself.
I’ll own this from here.
Let me summarize to make sure I’ve got it right…
I won’t transfer you again without staying on the line.
Here’s what I can do right now.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Agent apologizes once, summarizes accurately in under 20 seconds, sets clear next steps, and reduces agitation without blaming other teams.

scenarios.title: Hold and reconnect etiquette
scenarios.situation: Agent needs time to research and must place the customer on hold, with a plan if disconnected.
targetPhrases: Mind if I place you on a brief hold for about two minutes?
If we get disconnected, I’ll call you back at [number].
Thanks for hanging in there.
I’m back—thanks for your patience.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Agent asks permission with a time estimate, confirms callback number, returns within the estimate, and thanks the customer before resuming troubleshooting.

weeks.theme: Empathy that de-escalates without giving away the store

scenarios.title: Billing surprise: $49.99 charge
scenarios.situation: Customer reports an unexpected charge and is frustrated.
targetPhrases: I can see why that’s frustrating.
Let me pull up the charge and fix this.
Here’s what likely happened…
I’ll make this right.
Would a refund or account credit work better for you?
scenarios.successLooksLike: Agent validates once, explains in plain language, offers two concrete remedies, confirms preference, and documents the resolution.

scenarios.title: Wrong item—twice
scenarios.situation: Customer received the wrong product two times and is losing patience.
targetPhrases: You shouldn’t have to deal with this.
I’ll personally track this replacement.
I’m expediting shipping at no extra cost.
I’ll email the label while we’re on the line.
You’ll get an update by [time].
scenarios.successLooksLike: Agent takes ownership, upgrades shipping, provides a time-bound update, and sends the label before ending the call.

scenarios.title: Supervisor request—stabilize first
scenarios.situation: Customer demands a supervisor immediately.
targetPhrases: I can get a supervisor, and I’m also empowered to help.
Here’s what I can do right now while I bring them in.
Does that plan work for you?
I’ll stay with you on the line.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Agent acknowledges the request, proposes an immediate step within their authority, gains agreement, and performs a warm introduction if escalation proceeds.

weeks.theme: Call control and setting an agenda without sounding rigid

scenarios.title: Runaway story, focused fix
scenarios.situation: Customer gives a long backstory that risks derailing the call.
targetPhrases: Got it—let me make sure we solve this fast.
Here’s what we’ll tackle first…
I’ll take notes as we go.
Does that sound good?
scenarios.successLooksLike: Agent respectfully redirects, sets a two-step agenda, confirms buy-in, and keeps the customer talking to facts needed to solve the issue.

scenarios.title: Multi-issue triage
scenarios.situation: Customer brings three issues at once with limited time.
targetPhrases: Let’s prioritize the most urgent issue.
We’ll handle A now, then B if time allows.
If we run short, I’ll set a follow-up.
I want to respect your time.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Agent identifies priority, sequences items, and either resolves two or schedules a follow-up with clear ownership.

scenarios.title: Polite, purposeful interruption
scenarios.situation: Agent must interrupt to avoid wasted time.
targetPhrases: Sorry to jump in—I want to fix this quickly.
One quick question so I don’t waste your time…
Thanks—please go on.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Agent interrupts once with purpose, asks a precise question, and returns floor control smoothly.

scenarios.title: Login failure with step-by-step guidance
scenarios.situation: Customer cannot sign in; unclear error message.
targetPhrases: What happens when you try to sign in?
Let’s try this step by step together.
Please click Settings in the top right.
Tell me exactly what you see now.
I’ll stay with you while it loads.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Agent uses short, concrete directions, confirms each step, and avoids jargon while capturing the exact error text.

scenarios.title: When the customer says, “I already tried that”
scenarios.situation: Customer rejects standard steps as repeats.
targetPhrases: Thanks for trying that—let’s build on it.
Sometimes a small detail makes the difference.
Here’s a different angle we can try.
If it doesn’t work, we have a plan B.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Agent validates prior effort, reframes the step, proposes an alternate, and maintains momentum without arguing.

scenarios.title: Two-factor/OTP issues
scenarios.situation: Customer is not receiving or cannot read a one-time code.
targetPhrases: I’m sending a 6-digit code to your phone ending in ___.
Please read it back one number at a time.
If it doesn’t arrive, we’ll try email instead.
I’ll wait on the line.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Agent confirms destination, elicits slow, accurate read-back, and offers an immediate fallback channel.

weeks.theme: Policies, refunds, and alternatives that feel helpful

scenarios.title: Outside 30-day return window
scenarios.situation: Customer requests a refund past the stated policy.
targetPhrases: I want to help within our policy.
Here are the options I can offer today.
I can approve an exception this one time.
Would store credit get you what you need?
scenarios.successLooksLike: Agent states constraints once, offers at least two options, and secures agreement on the preferred path.

scenarios.title: Fee waiver request
scenarios.situation: Customer asks to waive a restocking or late fee.
targetPhrases: Given the circumstances, I can waive the fee.
I’ll document this so you’re covered.
You’ll see it on your account within 24 hours.
Anything else I can help with today?
scenarios.successLooksLike: Agent grants or denies with rationale, documents clearly, sets a timebound expectation, and closes cleanly.

scenarios.title: Saying no without burning goodwill
scenarios.situation: Requested action is not allowed.
targetPhrases: I wish I could do that.
Here’s what I can do right now.
Let’s figure out the next best step.
I want to keep this easy for you.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Agent declines once with empathy, pivots to alternatives, and keeps the customer engaged.

weeks.theme: Escalations, warm transfers, and rock-solid follow-through

scenarios.title: Warm transfer to Tier 2
scenarios.situation: Issue requires a specialist; customer dreads repeating the story.
targetPhrases: I’m bringing in a specialist.
Here’s a quick summary so you don’t repeat yourself.
I’m staying on the line until you’re connected.
Is it okay if I listen in?
scenarios.successLooksLike: Agent summarizes accurately in under 20 seconds, performs a warm handoff, and ensures ownership transfers clearly.

scenarios.title: Owning a callback
scenarios.situation: System outage prevents immediate fix; callback required.
targetPhrases: I’ll call you by [time] your local time.
If you don’t hear from me, here’s my direct line.
I’ll send a quick recap email after this call.
I appreciate your patience.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Agent commits to a precise time window, provides a backstop contact, sends a recap, and follows through on time.

scenarios.title: Notes that travel
scenarios.situation: Case may move between teams; notes must be actionable.
targetPhrases: I’ve added detailed notes to your case.
Any agent can pick this up without you repeating.
Your case number is ____.
I summarized the steps we tried.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Agent writes clear, structured notes with actions and results so the next agent can continue seamlessly.

weeks.theme: Handling anger, profanity, and threats to cancel

scenarios.title: Setting a respectful boundary
scenarios.situation: Customer uses profanity repeatedly.
targetPhrases: I want to help, and I can’t continue if the language stays this way.
Let’s keep this respectful so I can solve this.
I’m on your side.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Agent sets a boundary once, redirects to solutioning, and de-escalates without escalating tone.

scenarios.title: Save the account
scenarios.situation: Customer threatens to cancel immediately.
targetPhrases: I hear you. If we fix X today, would you stay?
Let me make this easy.
Here’s a solution I can offer now.
Does that work for you?
scenarios.successLooksLike: Agent identifies the root issue, proposes a concrete fix, and asks a clear save question.

scenarios.title: “This is false advertising”
scenarios.situation: Customer claims misleading marketing.
targetPhrases: I can see how it came across that way.
Let me walk you through what’s included.
If it still misses the mark, we’ll make it right.
Thanks for giving me a chance to fix this.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Agent acknowledges perception, clarifies features in plain language, and offers a remedy or path forward.

weeks.theme: US-style email and live chat that customers actually read

scenarios.title: Follow-up email with next steps
scenarios.situation: After-call recap required with actions and timelines.
targetPhrases: Subject: Quick recap and next steps
As promised, here’s what we did today…
Action needed from you:
You’re all set—no action needed.
Best regards, [Name], [Team]
scenarios.successLooksLike: Email has a clear subject, bullet points, bolded actions, dates in US format, and a friendly sign-off.

scenarios.title: Live chat pacing and tone
scenarios.situation: Customer engages via chat; expects fast, short messages.
targetPhrases: Hi, I’m [Name]. I’ll be your point of contact.
I’m reviewing your message now.
Thanks for your patience—still with me?
Glad we got this sorted. Anything else I can help with today?
scenarios.successLooksLike: Agent sends short, timely messages, checks presence after pauses, and closes with an offer to help further.

scenarios.title: Social DM to secure channel
scenarios.situation: Customer shares account info over social; must move to a private channel.
targetPhrases: For your privacy, let’s move to a secure channel.
Here’s a link to verify your account.
I’ll stay with you through the process.
Once verified, I’ll pick this up right away.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Agent moves the conversation securely without losing momentum and confirms next steps.

weeks.theme: Outages, no-ETA updates, and proactive communication

scenarios.title: System-wide outage—no ETA
scenarios.situation: Services are down for many customers; no exact timeline.
targetPhrases: We’re experiencing a wider outage.
Here’s what that means for you.
You don’t need to call back—I’ll own the update.
I’ll text you as soon as service is restored.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Agent explains impact, avoids false promises, sets a one-way update, and reduces repeat contacts.

scenarios.title: Proactive VIP update
scenarios.situation: High-value customer affected; call them before they call you.
targetPhrases: Just keeping you in the loop.
We’re on track for [timeframe].
Here’s a safe workaround for now.
I’ll follow up at [time].
scenarios.successLooksLike: Agent delivers a concise, proactive update with a workaround and a scheduled follow-up.

scenarios.title: Accountability without legal risk
scenarios.situation: Customer demands an apology and accountability.
targetPhrases: We fell short today.
No excuses—here’s what we’re doing about it.
Your experience matters to us.
Thanks for sticking with us.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Agent offers a sincere apology, names corrective actions, and maintains a professional tone.

weeks.theme: Soft sales in support: saves, cross-sells, and framing value

scenarios.title: Cancelation save by plan match
scenarios.situation: Customer wants to cancel due to cost or mismatch.
targetPhrases: What’s making you consider canceling?
If we could reduce your bill by X, would you stay?
Based on your usage, this plan fits better.
I’ll switch you over with no downtime.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Agent uncovers the why, offers a targeted alternative, confirms the save, and executes the change.

scenarios.title: Cross-sell during troubleshooting
scenarios.situation: Agent spots a product that prevents future issues.
targetPhrases: While we’re here, one thing that can prevent this is…
No pressure—just so you know.
Would you like me to add that for you?
Totally fine to skip—your call.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Agent asks permission, frames value briefly, and accepts yes/no without pressure.

scenarios.title: Framing value in US terms
scenarios.situation: Customer questions price or benefit.
targetPhrases: Here’s what you gain today…
This saves you about X hours a month.
Most customers like you choose…
You’re good to go.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Agent states outcomes, quantifies impact, uses social proof, and closes confidently.

weeks.theme: Sounding clear and natural to US ears: pronunciation and numbers

scenarios.title: Service phrases with US rhythm
scenarios.situation: Agents practice intonation, stress, and linking on high-use phrases.
targetPhrases: How can I help today?
Let me take care of that for you.
You’re all set.
Here’s what we’ll do.
Does that work for you?
Thanks for your patience.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Agent uses natural US stress and intonation, clear /v/ vs /b/, -ed endings, and smooth linking on core phrases.

scenarios.title: Spelling names, emails, and addresses
scenarios.situation: Capturing customer identity details accurately over the phone.
targetPhrases: That’s J as in Juliet, A as in Alpha…
Could you spell that for me, letter by letter?
Let me read that back to confirm.
Apartment or suite—just to double-check.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Agent uses a clear spelling alphabet, confirms back accurately, and avoids mishearing common letters and numbers.

scenarios.title: Numbers, prices, dates, and times (US format)
scenarios.situation: Quoting prices, dates, times, and order numbers accurately.
targetPhrases: That’s forty-nine ninety-nine.
The fifteenth of May, twenty twenty-six.
Two-thirty p.m. Pacific.
Zero vs. “oh” for clarity.
I’ll send it today, not tomorrow.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Agent speaks numbers and times clearly, confirms time zones, and avoids ambiguity that leads to rework.

weeks.theme: Capstone: end-to-end simulations and QA calibration

scenarios.title: Three-part call with transfer and callback
scenarios.situation: Login problem needs Tier 2; warm transfer fails; agent promises and delivers a callback.
targetPhrases: Let me summarize where we are…
Here’s the plan so you’re not left hanging.
I’m calling you back now as promised.
Thanks for sticking with me—we got it done.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Agent owns the case end-to-end, delivers a warm transfer, recovers from failure with an on-time callback, and confirms resolution.

scenarios.title: Review rescue call
scenarios.situation: Customer left a negative public review; agent calls to resolve and request an update.
targetPhrases: I saw your review and wanted to reach out personally.
I’m sorry we dropped the ball.
I’ve fixed X and here’s a goodwill gesture.
Would you be open to updating your review?
scenarios.successLooksLike: Agent acknowledges publicly stated pain, resolves the core issue, and asks for an update without pressure.

scenarios.title: Team QA calibration and peer coaching
scenarios.situation: Agents listen to recordings, align on what “good” sounds like, and coach each other’s phrasing.
targetPhrases: Let’s align on what good sounds like.
Here’s how I’d phrase that more clearly.
I appreciate the feedback—here’s my takeaway.
I’ll try that on my next call.
scenarios.successLooksLike: Agents use coaching language, capture action items, and align with the QA rubric for consistency.

successCriteria.plainLanguage: Agents open and close calls in a consistent, friendly US customer-service style.
successCriteria.measurableProxy: QA scorecards show 90%+ compliance with branded greeting, empathy on first contact, verification of two data points, and clear closing on 3 consecutive weeks.

successCriteria.plainLanguage: Escalated customers calm down and stay with us because agents use empathy and clear next steps.
successCriteria.measurableProxy: Supervisor escalations per 100 calls drop by 20% and CSAT on escalated calls improves by 0.3 points by week 8.

successCriteria.plainLanguage: Instructions and probing are clear enough that customers don’t get lost or ask for repeats.
successCriteria.measurableProxy: First Contact Resolution increases by 10% and average handle time decreases by 5% without an uptick in repeat contacts by week 10.

successCriteria.plainLanguage: Transfers and callbacks feel seamless and reliable to customers.
successCriteria.measurableProxy: 95% of escalations include a warm transfer with a summary in case notes; 95% of callbacks happen within the promised window.

successCriteria.plainLanguage: Emails and chats are concise, friendly, and easy to act on for US customers.
successCriteria.measurableProxy: Email/chat QA scores average 90%+ and grammar/spelling error rate is under 2 per 100 messages in weeks 9–12.

successCriteria.plainLanguage: Agents are easy to understand on the phone, especially with numbers, names, and addresses.
successCriteria.measurableProxy: In mock calls, repeat-back requests for names/numbers average under 1 per call; customer audits report 90%+ intelligibility by week 11.

kickoffMessage.en: Welcome to your 12-week Customer Support communication sprint. Our goal: help you sound natural and confident to US customers—clear words, friendly tone, and the right phrases at the right time. We’ll drill real call scenarios: long holds, multiple transfers, billing surprises, tough escalations, warm handoffs, and follow-ups that stick. Expect lots of speaking practice, feedback on tone and pronunciation, and quick wins you can use the same day. You’ll learn US-style openings and closings, empathy that calms, plain-English troubleshooting, polished emails and chats, and number/date clarity. Bring your toughest calls—we’ll turn them into playbooks. Let’s get you sounding crisp, warm, and “You’re all set.”
kickoffMessage.ko: 12주 고객지원 커뮤니케이션 스프린트에 오신 것을 환영합니다. 목표: 미국 고객에게 자연스럽고 자신감 있게 들리도록 돕는 것입니다—명확한 발음, 친근한 톤, 그리고 상황에 딱 맞는 표현. 실제 콜 상황으로 훈련합니다: 긴 대기 후 연결, 여러 번의 부서 이동, 결제 문제, 어려운 에스컬레이션, 매끄러운 연결(웜 트랜스퍼), 그리고 확실한 후속 조치. 말하기 연습과 톤/발음 피드백이 많고, 그날 바로 써먹을 수 있는 실전 표현을 익힙니다. 미국식 오프닝/클로징, 고객을 진정시키는 공감 표현, 쉬운 영어로 문제 해결, 깔끔한 이메일/채팅, 숫자·날짜를 정확히 전달하는 법을 배우게 됩니다. 가장 어려웠던 콜을 가져오세요—바로 우리 팀의 플레이북이 됩니다. 따뜻하면서도 또렷한 "You’re all set." 톤으로 함께 만들어 갑시다.
